# Environment Variables Demo

A `<Command>`, `<Check>` or `<Finish>` block's `env` prop sets environment variables for its script. Each value can use inputs and the outputs of other blocks, and reaches the script as data: nothing in it runs, whatever it holds. The block lists the values before you click Run, and instruction mode shows them as `export` lines.

## From inputs

<Inputs id="bucket">
```yaml
variables:
  - name: BucketName
    type: string
    description: Name of the bucket to plan
    default: my-demo-bucket
  - name: Copies
    type: int
    description: How many copies to keep
    default: 2
```
</Inputs>

<Command
  id="plan-bucket"
  title="Plan the bucket"
  inputsId="bucket"
  env={{ BUCKET: "{{ .inputs.BucketName }}", COPIES: "{{ .inputs.Copies }}", DRY_RUN: true }}
  command={`echo "Would create s3://$BUCKET with $COPIES copies (dry run: $DRY_RUN)"
echo "bucket=$BUCKET" >> "$RUNBOOK_OUTPUT"`}
/>

## From another block's outputs

`fetch-title` publishes a pull request title with shell syntax in it, as a title from an API can. `print-title` gets it as `$TITLE` and prints it as it is. Nothing in it runs.

<Command
  id="fetch-title"
  title="Fetch a pull request title"
  path="scripts/fetch-title.sh"
/>

<Check
  id="print-title"
  title="Print the title"
  env={{ TITLE: "{{ .outputs.fetch_title.title }}" }}
  path="checks/print-title.sh"
/>

### Entering an output by hand

Each output an env value reads is a chip in the block's list of variables. Before `fetch-title` runs, the `TITLE` chip names the output `print-title` waits for. Click it, type a title in its place and press Enter, and `print-title` can run without `fetch-title`. The reset button next to the title brings the chip back.

## Only for that block

The variables are the block's own. The next block doesn't see `TITLE`.

<Check
  id="title-is-gone"
  title="Check that TITLE is gone"
  command='test -z "${TITLE:-}"'
/>
